title: Efficient Security Support for CXL Memory through Adaptive Incremental Offloaded (Re-)Encryption
problem: CXL memory expansion devices adopted in cloud TEE environments (Intel SGX/TDX, AMD SEV) require XTS encryption for data confidentiality via CXL IDE, but XTS encryption's per-page latency causes significant performance overhead on memory-intensive workloads. Dynamically switching between CTR and XTS encryption modes and re-encrypting pages when access frequency changes incurs additional overhead that existing designs do not handle efficiently.
motivation: CXL memory is increasingly deployed in cloud computing to expand DRAM bandwidth and capacity, but integrating it into TEE-protected enclaves creates a security overhead bottleneck that limits adoption in latency-sensitive workloads.
method: AIORE speeds up encrypted access to CXL memory expansion devices by using two different encryption methods depending on how often data is accessed. Frequently accessed pages (hot pages) use CTR encryption, which is fast and can run in parallel, while rarely accessed pages (cold pages) use XTS encryption, which is required by the CXL IDE security standard. When a page's usage pattern changes, AIORE re-encrypts only that single page, doing the work using compute resources inside the CXL memory device itself so the re-encryption happens in parallel with regular memory traffic. This approach is tested using gem5 full-system simulation across diverse workloads.
key_novelty: The key advance is offloading incremental page re-encryption to the CXL memory device's own compute, enabling dynamic switching between CTR and XTS encryption modes based on access frequency.
contributions: Adaptive encryption policy that dynamically assigns CTR or XTS encryption per page based on access frequency, reducing XTS overhead on hot pages
Incremental re-encryption strategy that limits re-encryption to changed pages rather than full memory regions
Offloading of re-encryption computation to the CXL memory node, hiding re-encryption latency behind normal memory traffic
Security overhead reduced by 62.8% on average with overhead within 3.7% relative to insecure baseline (gem5 evaluation)

metrics.other: Security overhead reduced by 62.8% on average; overhead within 3.7% vs. insecure baseline (gem5)

baselines: CXL IDE with XTS-only encryption (baseline secure)
limitations: Evaluation is simulation-based (gem5); hardware implementation and area/power costs of the CXL node compute for re-encryption are not discussed.
primary_theme: adaptive encryption for CXL memory in trusted execution environments
